disposition_reason: Reports mean ± SD lead, cadmium, copper, zinc, iron and manganese in canned pork and beef and in meat pies from five Polish meat factories.

study.design: retail survey of canned meat and meat pies by manufacturer
study.method: dry ashing at 550 °C, HCl dissolution; Pb and Cd by non-flame (graphite furnace) AAS, Cu, Zn, Fe, Mn by flame AAS (AA-880)
study.qa: no CRM, recovery or blanks reported

controls.control: product type (meat pie with liver/kidney vs canned meat)
controls.outcome: Authors state meat pies contained 33.3% more cadmium than canned meat and generally more lead (Table 3)

unresolved: Number of samples (cans/pies) per factory not stated; n left null.
Meat pie row for the fifth factory is printed '-' (not analysed); no finding recorded.
Text gives two different lead limits (0.30 mg/kg p. 19 and 0.10 mg/kg p. 20).
Text says meat pie Cd ranged 0.038-0.040 mg/kg, which does not match Table 3 (0.026-0.106); table values used.
Table 3 canned row header reads 'Konserwy wieprzowo-mięsne' vs 'wieprzowo-wołowe' in Tables 1-2; same product group assumed.
DOI is not printed in the PDF; manifest DOI 10.2478/v10083-010-0003-0 used.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Polish Minister of Health Decree 13 Jan 2003 maximum levels quoted: Pb 0.30 mg/kg, Cd 0.05 mg/kg in food; Cd 0.1 mg/kg in meat products containing liver and kidneys; text later cites Pb limit 0.10 mg/kg
